page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is a high-performance computing server powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz with a single thread per core configuration. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and does not include integrated GPUs. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 147,294.74. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with uncached large-block read speeds reaching 695.05 GB/sec and write speeds at 347.3 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. The processor's extended instruction capabilities, including AVX-512 and vector neural network instructions (AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16), contribute to strong performance in physics simulations and software compilation, where it scored 59,439.0 in Clang compilation tests.

Given its high memory-to-core ratio of 16 GB per core and dedicated non-hyperthreaded execution units, this server offers a resource-dense profile optimized for parallel processing without resource contention. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs indicates a design tailored for network-attached storage architectures and CPU-bound calculations. It is highly suited for high-performance computing (HPC) workloads, large-scale scientific simulations, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and memory-intensive database operations.
